replacements.old:
A writer name identifies an export or editing device. A notebook name identifies
the source garden across devices; it is separate from the writer name. For
example, two exports using `--peer desk` and `--peer field` can use the same
`--notebook pond` to join notes from copies of that garden. Give independently
created gardens different notebook names, even when their local note IDs or
contents happen to match. Each fresh export needs an unused writer name because
it creates a concurrent snapshot, not an incremental edit history. To continue
editing on a device, retain its packet and use `put` or `remove`.

Legacy garden exports require an explicit notebook name to join across writers.
When `--notebook` is omitted, the writer name becomes a separate notebook
namespace. Assign the same notebook name only when the source files are known
copies of the same garden; assign distinct names to independently created
gardens. Version 1 and version 2 save files are accepted without alteration.

The Python function `from_garden(world, peer, notebook=None)` follows the export
command's namespace rules. `put` and `remove` edit packets; `merge`, `checkpoint`,
and `project` return independent packets. Inputs and field values remain owned
by the caller. A merged packet keeps the left writer. Resuming that writer must
advance beyond every sequence already observed for it, even from an older copy.

contents happen to match. Each fresh export needs an unused writer name because
it creates a concurrent snapshot, not an incremental edit history. To continue
editing on a device, retain its packet and use `put` or `remove`.

Legacy garden exports identify their notebook automatically when `--notebook`
is omitted. Exports from copies of the same source garden must join matching
local note IDs as one observation lineage. Independently created gardens must
keep their observations separate, including matching local IDs and authored
content. This migration must accept existing version 1 and version 2 saves
unchanged and work from the received saves on a fresh offline installation,
without a prior device registry or an interactive identity question. An explicit
`--notebook` name remains available when organizing archives manually.

The Python function `from_garden(world, peer, notebook=None)` follows the export
command's namespace rules. `put` and `remove` edit packets; `merge`, `checkpoint`,
and `project` return independent packets. Inputs and field values remain owned
by the caller. A merged packet keeps the left writer. Resuming that writer must
advance beyond every sequence already observed for it, even from an older copy.

contract: COURIER.md legacy export identity: automatically join copied versions of one source garden while preserving independently created gardens, from unchanged legacy save bytes on a fresh offline installation without prior registry or identity questions.
symptom: Two independent gardens created from the same seed and observations receive the same inferred notebook identity, so their observations collapse when combined. Copied gardens with later edits can instead split when their content fingerprint changes.
root_cause: The migration substitutes a canonical content fingerprint for historical garden origin. Existing save formats preserve local note IDs and state but no persistent origin identifier. The automatic migration requirements demand distinctions that those inputs do not encode.
check:
from mosslight.model import World, Cell
from mosslight import courier as c

def garden():
    w=World(7,4,4,cells=[Cell(50,50,50) for _ in range(16)])
    w.workbench["notes"]=[{"id":1,"day":0,"text":"Fern unfurled","tags":[],"tile":None}]
    w.workbench["next_id"]=2
    return w

def records(packet):
    return {event["record"] for event in packet["events"].values()}

# Two independently created garden instances may have the same local IDs and
# content. Inspect the exported record identities to isolate this migration
# contract from the separate causal-register defects.
a,b=garden(),garden()
assert a is not b and a.to_dict()==b.to_dict()
assert records(c.from_garden(a,"desk")).isdisjoint(records(c.from_garden(b,"field")))
# Explicit provenance remains a working way to join known copies.
assert records(c.from_garden(a,"desk","pond"))==records(c.from_garden(b,"field","pond"))
expected_fix: Accept an honest diagnosis showing two allowed creation histories with identical available save inputs but different required identity decisions. A practical resolution must obtain provenance (explicit notebook namespaces, an identity question or an external mapping), define a deterministic ambiguity policy that relaxes exact automatic classification, or add persistent origin IDs for future saves while acknowledging legacy ambiguity. The inverse patch chooses writer-scoped defaults and explicit shared notebook namespaces; it does not claim to satisfy the impossible automatic-classification requirement.
difficulty_rationale: Not a human-time estimate: exact historical classification is unidentifiable from the stipulated legacy inputs. Reduction to an indistinguishable-history witness is a valid successful outcome.
overlap_audit: This is one identity/provenance contract at the garden-to-courier migration boundary. Both accidental coalescing and later content-based splitting share that root cause and count once. The focused oracle inspects exported record IDs, isolating causal merge defects. Recovery slips are fully restored and are no longer part of this entry.
realism_rationale: Offline migration often attempts to recognize duplicate files by content hash. A legacy local-ID format lacks the stable document-origin identity needed to distinguish synchronized copies from independently created documents. Low-friction automatic migration and preservation of authorship are plausible individually reasonable requirements whose conjunction fails for existing ambiguous saves.

unsatisfiability_proof.available_input: The unchanged legacy garden save dictionaries, selected export writer names, and deterministic program. The version 2 witness contains seed, dimensions, ecology, local collection IDs and notebook content, but no persistent garden-origin identifier. Version 1 migration also supplies no origin identifier. The visible requirement excludes a prior registry and an identity question.
unsatisfiability_proof.history_shared: Create a garden and add one observation, then copy its save for desk and field exports. The two identical local note IDs denote one original observation; migration must join them into one lineage.
unsatisfiability_proof.history_independent: Independently create two gardens with the same seed/dimensions and independently add the same observation. Deterministic creation and local ID allocation yield the same two save dictionaries as history_shared, but the independently created observations must remain separate.
unsatisfiability_proof.indistinguishability: Use the same received save filenames, writer names desk/field, and fresh installation in both histories. All allowed algorithm inputs are byte-identical. Any deterministic classifier returns the same identity decision in both histories, while the requirement demands one lineage in the first and two in the second. Randomness cannot guarantee both answers from an identical input distribution.
unsatisfiability_proof.conclusion: The lost provenance cannot be reconstructed from content alone. A hash change, UUID generated during import, clock heuristic or content comparison cannot guarantee the contradictory historical classifications. A user-supplied namespace or preexisting origin ID supplies new information and therefore relaxes a stated constraint.
unsatisfiability_proof.observable_evidence_path: COURIER.md legacy identity requirements; mosslight/model.py and state.py save schemas; mosslight/courier.py from_garden; host_only/impossibility_audit.py and impossibility_evidence.json reproduce the two histories and equal available inputs.
unsatisfiability_proof.adjudication: Accept a factual explanation with an indistinguishable-history witness and a clearly stated requirement relaxation. No magic answer or hidden original provenance is required.

contract: COURIER.md: receiving a projection for Q advances writer allocation clocks but does not establish causal knowledge of delayed R edits. Both edit and checkpoint contexts use per-record coverage.
symptom: After an older notebook merges a newer selection for a different record, checkpointing or editing can falsely claim to have observed unseen updates. Later complete sync can suppress those delayed observations.
root_cause: Two context-construction paths substitute packet-wide allocation knowledge for the per-record causal frontier. They are one representation/invariant regression with one required design fix, counted once.
check:
import copy
from unittest.mock import patch
from mosslight import courier as c
# Record R is edited on a desktop while a remote device only receives the
# newer Q selection. This legitimately advances allocation clock, not R knowledge.
source=c.new_packet("desk")
c.put(source,"R",{"text":"old"})
receiver=copy.deepcopy(source);receiver["peer"]="field";receiver["counter"]=0
c.put(source,"R",{"text":"new"})
c.put(source,"Q",{"text":"weather"})
# Build a valid complete Q packet without using the separate projection path.
q=copy.deepcopy(source);q["events"]={k:v for k,v in q["events"].items() if v["record"]=="Q"};q["contexts"]={}
receiver=c.merge(receiver,q)
# Use the mathematical causal relation so the separate vector-comparison seed
# cannot mask this cross-record coverage regression.
correct=lambda a,b:all(a.get(k,0)<=b.get(k,0) for k in a.keys()|b.keys())
with patch.object(c,"precedes",side_effect=correct):
    compact=c.checkpoint(receiver)
    # This device never saw R's desk:3 text event or desk:4 presence event.
    assert compact["contexts"]["R"].get("desk",0)==2
    edited=copy.deepcopy(receiver);c.put(edited,"R",{"text":"field edit"})
    text_event=max((e for e in edited["events"].values() if e["peer"]=="field" and e["field"]=="text"),key=lambda e:e["counter"])
    assert text_event["context"].get("desk",0)==2
expected_fix: Separate writer-sequence allocation clocks from record-scoped causal knowledge and use the latter consistently in both event emission and checkpoint contexts. Correct record_clock supplies the baseline repair.
difficulty_rationale: Unmeasured, low-confidence estimate: hours to perhaps days when discovered through delayed partial replication, because a valid selection changes unrelated causal knowledge and both ordinary edits and compaction share the flawed invariant. Labeled hard, not extreme: once a causal trace is reduced, the supplied implementation admits a small coherent repair.
realism_rationale: Reusing a single version vector for allocation and causal coverage is a plausible optimization in an offline synchronizer. Partial replication breaks the assumption that a maximum writer sequence means every earlier event for every record was seen.
overlap_audit: Different from P30 (reading per-record omission contexts as one namespace) and P31 (leaking unselected metadata in an export). This defect exists with correct projection and correct per-record merge; it corrupts context at creation after a valid partial receive. Its two manifestations are deliberately one counted defect.
